{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — APCN 2 Construction & Maintenance Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (for the Customer, Teleglobe USA Inc.) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the APCN 2 C&MA — verified findings, walk-away items and next steps

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed 18 playbook rules against the Agreement. Nine clauses are compliant (several sitting at the fallback), seven are deviations requiring redline, and two rules are unmet with no usable clause in the document.

The structural point driving most of the risk is that this is a multilateral consortium construction and maintenance agreement rather than a vendor supply contract, so several protections we normally take for granted are simply absent. Where the consortium bargain is symmetrical it generally works in our favour and we do not redline it: liability is mutual, several and not joint, with no aggregate cap (so indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct exposure is already uncapped); assignment to successors, parents, subsidiaries and affiliates is available on notice with no change-of-control trigger; we take Allocated Capacity on an ownership basis with unrestricted IRU and resale rights; and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN or non-solicitation obligation binding us.

The deviations cluster on exit, cost commitment and supplier accountability. There is no IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the Agreement; Paragraph 4.9 disclaims all warranties, leaving us effectively "as is"; Paragraph 18 locks us into a 25-year initial period with no convenience exit; Paragraphs 7.1/7.2 commit us to uncapped Schedule B cost shares for that period; Subparagraph 23.2 forfeits everything we have paid on a three-month payment default; the Paragraph 9 audit right is unlimited in frequency and requires no notice; and Subparagraph 27.2 affirmatively directs courts and tribunals to disregard the facts identifying the applicable law, with the Management Committee procedure as our "sole and exclusive remedy". Seven of these sit in playbook walk-away territory and are set out below.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | KDD T8 | Only consortium cost-sharing indemnities (21.2, Para 32); no IP infringement indemnity, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no super-cap. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | KDD T8 | Outright ownership of Allocated Capacity (12.2, 4.1, 4.3) exceeds the fallback licence; unrestricted exploitation under 12.20 and 12.22. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | KDD T8 | Mutual exclusion (21.3), several not joint (21.1), no aggregate cap so fallback carve-outs are met structurally; sits at fallback. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | KDD T8 | 22.3(a)–(d) permit successor/parent/subsidiary/affiliate transfer on notice (22.6); no change-of-control provision. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 | No sourcing restriction; 12.20, 12.22 and 17.2–17.4 run in our favour. Preferred position met. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties on Customer | Deviation | KDD T8 | 23.2 forfeits all amounts paid and denies any credit on a three-month payment default (23.1) — penalty unrelated to actual loss. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | KDD T8 (§ 35 Entire Agreement) | Capacity/IRU regime at or above fallback: affiliate use (12.8, 12.14), successor transfer (22.3(a), Para 30), not revocable at discretion. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 | No restrictive covenant; pro-competitive provisions (12.20, 12.22, 17.4) benefit us. Preferred position met. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | KDD T8 | 18.1 imposes a 25-year initial period with exit only at or after its end on one year's notice; 18.2 requires unanimity or a 90% majority. No Customer convenience exit. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | KDD T8 | 9.8 audit right is unlimited in frequency with no notice; 9.9 adds no limit. Cost recovery already at or above fallback. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | KDD T8 | No governing law designated; 27.2 directs tribunals to disregard identifying facts; 27.1 makes the Management Committee the sole and exclusive remedy with no seat or venue. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 | No MFN binds us; 15.2 and 17.2 are MFN-style undertakings owed by Terminal Parties, of which we are not one. Preserve. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments on Customer | Deviation | KDD T8 | 7.1/7.2 Schedule B cost shares locked in by 18.1 for 25+ years, uncapped, no in-term reduction, with 23.1 reclamation on non-payment. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 (§ 35 Entire Agreement) | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere. Preferred position met. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | KDD T8 | 18.1 is a single 25-year term then open-ended; no auto-renewal and no renewal price uplift, so both fallback triggers are absent. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | KDD T8 | Para 18 and 23.3 address assets, decommissioning and liquidation only; no migration assistance and no data return or export obligation. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | KDD T8 | 4.9 disclaims all representations and warranties (Supplier performance, Wet Segment reliability, integration); no warranty period or remedy. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | KDD T8 | 5.3 makes insurance permissive and the cost definitions expressly allow self-insurance "in lieu of insurance"; no minimum limits, E&O, cyber or certificates. |

---

## Walk-away items

These seven deviations fall into playbook walk-away territory and should be resolved before signature:

1. **No supplier IP indemnity (INDEMN, KDD T8).** The Agreement contains no infringement or intellectual-property language at all. We propose a new Subparagraph 21.4 at the fallback level only: an IP infringement indemnity from the supplying Party, customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual O&M Costs super-cap. We deliberately do not reopen the mutual 21.2/Para 32 bargain, which also benefits us.
2. **Penalty forfeiture on payment default (LD, Subparagraph 23.2).** Reclamation of our entire allocated capacity with no payment or credit, plus forfeiture of every amount already paid, on a three-month default. We delete the no-credit denial and the forfeiture, leaving reclamation and accrued-account liability intact.
3. **No Customer convenience exit in a multi-year term (T4C, Paragraph 18).** We insert Subparagraph 18.1A: the Customer may terminate the Agreement or its participation for convenience on not more than 30 days' prior written notice, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. The counterparty side of the rule is already satisfied and is not redrafted.
4. **Unlimited, unannounced audits (AUDIT, Paragraph 9).** We add a new 9.10 carrying the two missing fallback mechanics only — once per calendar year and 15 days' prior written notice — leaving 9.8 and 9.9 verbatim, since the cost-recovery position already exceeds the fallback.
5. **No governing law and no court recourse (GOVLAW, Subparagraphs 27.1 and 27.2).** We take the preferred position: New York law and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, and conform 27.1 so the Management Committee step is an escalation procedure rather than the sole and exclusive remedy. Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the London courts remain acceptable fallbacks.
6. **Uncapped 25-year spend commitment (MINCOMMIT, Subparagraphs 7.1, 7.2, 18.1, 23.1).** We insert Subparagraph 7.2A at the fallback: O&M commitment confined to the then-current 12-month period from the RFS Date, reducible on 30 days' notice, settled at our proportionate share of O&M Costs actually incurred with actual-cost true-up and no penalty, forfeiture, reclamation or acceleration. We do not seek the preferred level, which would mean abandoning Schedule B proportionate cost-bearing.
7. **Effectively "as is" (WARRANTY, Paragraph 4.9).** We insert Subparagraph 4.10 — 90 days software conformance to documentation, 30 days services, with repair, replacement or refund — and carve it out of the 4.9 disclaimer so the retained disclaimer does not swallow it.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven walk-away deviations above plus the two gap-fillers: Subparagraph 18.8 (90 days' transition assistance to Teleglobe and export of its data within 30 days of expiry or termination) and mandatory E&O of at least USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of at least USD 2,000,000 on the other APCN 2 Parties. Both gap-fillers are drafted to run in our favour only so they do not create new obligations on us.
2. **Prioritise negotiation** in the order INDEMN, WARRANTY, GOVLAW, T4C, MINCOMMIT, LD, AUDIT — the first three go to whether we have any accountability or forum at all.
3. **Hold the compliant positions.** Do not trade away the mutual liability regime (no aggregate cap benefits us as much as it exposes us), the notice-only assignment rights, outright capacity ownership with unrestricted resale, or the Terminal Party MFN and non-discrimination undertakings in 15.2 and 17.2, of which we are a beneficiary.
4. **Diligence items flagged in the rationales, not redlined:** (a) confirm the I&ASC's IRU guidelines and IRU agreement terms under 12.23 do not narrow affiliate or contractor use, relying on "No provisions of the IRU agreement shall override the provisions of this Agreement"; (b) note that the retained sentence denying capital-cost credit is keyed to Subparagraph 18.1 alone and cannot attach to a withdrawal under our new 18.1A; (c) note that under 5.3 and the cost definitions an uninsured loss suffered by another Party is recharged in part to us.
5. **Business input required** on the 12-month O&M reduction mechanic in 7.2A and on whether we will press the preferred insurance limits (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation and certificates) if the counterparties show flexibility.
6. **Escalate for approval to sign** only once the seven walk-away items are at or above fallback; three carry critical or high severity."}
